names.status: A room shows the name {tool} gives each session, so you can match it to the terminal or window it runs in. A name can be a title {tool} wrote from your conversation. Atlas keeps the last names it read in memory until you switch names or the session list off, or quit the app; it never writes them to a file or a log, sends them anywhere, or gives them to an agent.
names.off: Atlas does not read session names. Rooms call a session by its tool and number, such as {example}.
names.needsList: Session names come from the session list, which is off.

bySession.label: Sessions at work
bySession.about: Each agent session is shown once, with what it says of itself and the folders it works in. Commits and uncommitted files belong to a folder, not to a session: where sessions share a folder, Atlas cannot tell which one changed a file, so that folder's changes are shown once, when you press it. Only sessions working in this repository's folders are shown. Memory and CPU on a session are its own program's and the commands it started, wherever they run, so they hold even in a shared folder.

pulse.status: While Workshop is open, macOS tells Atlas each time a file changes in one of this repository's worktrees, and Atlas counts the changes. It does not open the files and keeps no file name. Changes inside .git and to files Git ignores are not counted. Counts stay in memory for an hour.

load.status: Every 5 seconds while Workshop is open, Atlas reads how much memory and CPU each agent and the commands it started are using, the memory and CPU of a Java program outside them, such as a Gradle daemon, and how busy this Mac's memory, CPU and GPU are. It reads each program's name, never its command line. Nothing is written and nothing leaves this Mac.
load.off: Atlas does not read memory, CPU or GPU use, so no room or heading shows them.

about.body: One room is one worktree: a separate folder of this repository where a branch is being worked on. Each screen shows the branch, its newest commits and the files changed but not committed yet. A room is lit while an agent session is working in it. Press a room to see the rest.

tower.adviceMemory: macOS reports memory pressure as {pressure}. {name} holds the most: {memory}.
tower.failed: Atlas could not read this computer's load just now and tries again in 5 seconds.
tower.windows: On Windows, Atlas does not read this computer's load yet, so it does not judge it. Worktrees and sessions still show.
tower.about: Atlas compares the work waiting for the CPU, macOS's average over the last minute, with this computer's cores, and judges memory by macOS's own pressure level. Busy: more work than cores, or memory pressure high. Overloaded: 2.5 times the work the cores can run, or memory pressure critical. The fit is the worktrees running work times 2.5, divided by how many times over the cores the last 5 minutes ran; other programs' work counts against them too. A subagent with no worktree of its own runs inside its session's program and is counted there.
tower.sessionNever: Atlas does not stop agent sessions. To stop one, press Esc or Ctrl-C in its own window, where you can see what it was doing.

leftover.button: Stop {count, plural, one {# leftover process} other {# leftover processes}} ({memory})
leftover.note: Each one kept running after whatever started it ended, its folder was removed or its branch merged, and it has no terminal or child process. Stopping asks each to quit; nothing else is touched.
leftover.done: {count, plural, one {# process quit.} other {# processes quit.}}
leftover.changed: Nothing was stopped: these processes changed after the list was drawn. The list is updated.

remove.title: Remove {branch}'s worktree?
remove.body: It is merged into {base} and has no uncommitted changes. Git deletes the folder with its ignored files. The branch stays, and git worktree add brings the folder back.
remove.others: These ignored files are deleted too, and Atlas cannot tell whether a build makes them again: {paths}

build.backgroundNote: It keeps running at the lowest priority, with slower disk and network, so other work finishes first. The load stays the same, since the build still runs. Press again to set it back.
